answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/upi/accept-a-payment identifies UPI acceptance in India using Payment Intents and Payment Methods APIs and indexes Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions, and Elements with Payment Intents (new raw lines 5-16). It contains no detailed prerequisites or state transitions. The May 6 guide says the customer authenticates on mobile and approves a payment or future charges. Checkout uses INR line items, supports payment, setup and subscription, and refers to UPI AutoPay e-mandates. The merchant gets immediate stated success/failure notification for one-off and saving cases and a delayed notification for absent-customer off-session or recurring payments (old raw lines 18-49). In May Checkout, the QR expires after five minutes and triggers the failure event (old raw lines 104-114). In the May Elements routes, the merchant server creates either a Session or an Intent; the client uses the matching object and client secret to confirm, and the Intent route retrieves status on return. A return may show succeeded, processing or a failed state and does not itself verify payment (old raw lines 139-174, 502-541, 603-647, 866-868 and 962-1017). source-stripe-upi-accept-payment.md captures these three routes but adds a Direct API fourth variant not in either acceptance capture.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/upi/accept-a-payment, the November change is presentational and navigational (new raw lines 9-16), with no substantive operation or prerequisite demonstrated. source-stripe-upi-accept-payment.md lines 13 and 17 list a fourth path the May acceptance capture did not contain (old raw lines 8-115, 116-581 and 582-1081). Retain the distinct May Direct API evidence for saving UPI in raw/stripe-upi-set-up-future-payments-2025.md lines 109-121 and 341-374. It does not show a missing November acceptance body or a removed integration. Preserve May INR and e-mandate mode limits, immediate one-off and saving versus delayed absent-customer notifications, the five-minute Checkout QR and failure event, and the independent 24-hour Session lifespan in the Elements with Checkout Sessions guide (old raw lines 18-49, 104-114 and 139-143). Preserve the root index line 7, Stripe index lines 367 and 748, and Real-Time Payments concept line 203 routes, add the source backlink and keep the November raw as navigation. The concept's dated future-payments evidence should remain visible alongside the separate table's unspecified labels.
